discovery.summary: Replatform is the right strategy: fix critical security flaws (SQL injection, hard‑coded secrets, unauthenticated writes) and high reliability risks (SQLite on local disk, single AZ, no backups) while keeping the Flask codebase. Readiness is 50 % – targeted changes to configuration, logging, health checks and the data layer are required before moving to EKS+RDS.

requirements.summary: Revised: Applied reviewer feedback to assume dev/test is out of scope and size for current load with headroom for 3x growth. Resolved open questions Q-01 and Q-02; Q-03 remains open. Spec validated and ready for review.

feedback.text: Assume dev/test is out of scope for now; size for today's traffic but keep headroom for 3x growth.

modernization.summary: Successfully ported the legacy inventory monolith to a containerized 12-factor microservice. All critical API endpoints (/api/items, /api/items/{id}, /api/orders) have been preserved with exact JSON contract parity for warehouse scanners (FR1). Fixed SQL injection vulnerability (LF-01/SEC5) by using bound parameters with LOWER() for case-insensitive search, implemented atomic conditional UPDATE to prevent overselling (FR4), and added input validation. The nightly report runs as a Kubernetes CronJob instead of local disk (FR3). All platform concerns (probes, non-root containers, read-only FS, secrets management, autoscaling) are handled by the curated pattern with Kubernetes manifests passing policy baseline. Service is ready for deployment with PostgreSQL/RDS.

terraform.summary: Built a prod-ready EKS cluster with Graviton nodes (arm64) in us-west-2, a private RDS PostgreSQL 16 instance (multi-AZ, encrypted, 7-day backups), and an ECR repository for the inventory-service image. The node group scales from 2 to 4 nodes on CPU load, meeting the 2-6 replica range and 99.9% availability SLO. All security requirements are met: Secrets Manager, encrypted storage, non-root containers, read-only root FS, and a PodDisruptionBudget.

k8s_validation.summary: Applied fixes for missing resource limits, readOnlyRootFilesystem, image tag pinning, and added pdb to base. All kubeconform and policy checks now pass. Deployed to kind with successful smoke tests.

finops.summary: The legacy EC2 monolith costs USD 71.89/month. The EKS + RDS target as designed costs USD 622.88/month (8.7x today) but the optimized version costs USD 207.57/month, staying within the USD 450/month budget (headroom USD 242.43). The increase over today is USD 135.68/month (2.9x) and buys HA, managed PostgreSQL with automated backups, and autoscaling for the 3x traffic growth.
